title: Parallel Future Backend using mizu
text: future.mizu package backend future framework, also known Futureverse. Futureverse makes easy parallelize existing R code - often minor change code. users interact via higher-level packages futurize, future.apply, furrr, doFuture, choose code runs setting future backend plan(). package adds mizu_multisession backend, runs futures parallel local machine using mizu package. thing differs using future backend plan() call. code change, gives identical results, behaves exactly .
code: library(futurize) plan(future.mizu::mizu_multisession)  # parallelize on the current machine  # A slow function slow_fcn <- function(x) {   Sys.sleep(1.0)   x^2 }  # Example data xs <- 1:10  # Sequential and parallel base R apply ys <- lapply(xs, slow_fcn) ys <- lapply(xs, slow_fcn) |> futurize()  # Sequential and parallel purrr map library(purrr) ys <- xs |> map(slow_fcn) ys <- xs |> map(slow_fcn) |> futurize()  # Sequential and parallel foreach calls library(foreach) ys <- foreach(x = xs) %do% slow_fcn(x) ys <- foreach(x = xs) %do% slow_fcn(x) |> futurize()

title: Parallel Future Backend using mizu
text: mizu package runs parallel R workers local machine. Instead communicating via sockets, main R process workers exchange data via shared memory - POSIX shared memory Linux macOS, Win32 file mappings Windows.

title: Parallel Future Backend using mizu
text: Communication main R process workers cheap, means work can split many small futures without overhead dominating. Large vectors data frames read workers place, without worker holding copy. works Linux, macOS, Windows, requires additional setup.

title: Parallel Future Backend using mizu
text: workers always run local machine. workers machines, high-performance compute (HPC) cluster, use another future backend, e.g. plan(cluster) future.batchtools. 64 workers supported mizu. Data passed via shared memory, limited size. instance, Docker containers default 64 MB shared memory, might enough passing large objects. Cancelling future advisory. future already running worker interrupted; runs completion result discarded. Using single worker, plan(future.mizu::mizu_multisession, workers = 1), falls back sequential processing current R process, unless number workers protected (), e.g. workers = (1).

title: Mizu-based localhost multisession futures — mizu_multisession
code: library(future) plan(future.mizu::mizu_multisession)  # A function that returns a future # (note that N is a global variable) f <- function() future({   4 * sum((runif(N) ^ 2 + runif(N) ^ 2) < 1) / N }, seed = TRUE)  # Run a simple sampling approximation of pi in parallel using  M * N points: N <- 1e6  # samples per worker M <- 10   # iterations pi_est <- Reduce(sum, Map(value, replicate(M, f()))) / M print(pi_est) #> [1] 3.141674  ## Switch back to sequential processing, which also ## shuts down the automatically launched mizu workers  plan(sequential)
